column1: # tests/run-tasks-models.tsv - model seats offered by run-tasks-batch.ps1.
# A row belongs here only if tests/test-toolcalls.ps1 measured PASS for that
# tag on the listed host(s) (see docs/start-here.md + AGENTS.md Gotchas -
# failing models like the qwen2.5-coder / deepseek-r1 / glm4 families are
# never offered as seats). run-tasks-batch.ps1 reads this and intersects it
# with what each live host serves (the engine adapter's served-model list), so:
#   - adding a new tool-capable model = one row here, the script is never edited
#   - a host that is down, or a tag not served there yet, stops being offered
# Columns: tag<TAB>engine<TAB>hosts<TAB>desc. engine = ollama | llamacpp |
# opencode-go: the serving engine, and with a host the seat's provider
# (ollama-<host>/<tag>, llamacpp-<host>/<tag>). One tag on two engines is two
# rows, because a probe PASS is evidence for one engine only. hosts =
# whitespace-separated host tokens (desktop | node3 | server) matching the
# OLLAMA_<HOST>_BASE_URL / LLAMACPP_<HOST>_BASE_URL env each profile exports.
# Hosted seats are the exception: engine `opencode-go`, host token `opencode-go`,
# means the OpenCode Go
# subscription (model id opencode-go/<tag>), billed per token. Those rows were
# smoke-tested, NOT probed - the probe covers local engines only - each one wrote a
# file through `opencode run --auto` on 2026-10-06, and the owner approved them
# as seats. run-tasks-batch.ps1 offers one only when `opencode models
# opencode-go` lists it, the API key file exists and the live config resolves;
# never under 'all' (use -Models hosted, or name it), and never above its spend
# cap (-SpendCapShare of the monthly allowance in costs/go-rates.tsv; a seat with
# no rate row there is refused).
